verses.1: Having heard the words spoken by Agastya, Rama was filled with astonishment, wondering how the Rakshasas could have originated in Lanka in ancient times.
verses.2: Then, shaking his head and repeatedly looking at Agastya, whose body resembled the three sacred fires, Rama smiled and spoke to him.
verses.3: O revered one, having heard your statement that this Lanka formerly belonged to the flesh-eaters, a great astonishment has arisen within me.
verses.4: We have heard that the Rākṣasas originated from Pulastya's lineage, but now you have also spoken of their origin from another source.
verses.5: Are these new Rākṣasas indeed more powerful than Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa, Prahasta, Vikaṭa, and even Rāvaṇa's own sons?
verses.6: O Brāhmaṇa, who was their first ancestor, what was his name, and how were these exceedingly powerful beings driven away by Viṣṇu after committing what offense?
verses.7: O sinless one, please narrate all of this to me in detail and dispel my great curiosity, just as the sun dispels darkness.
verses.8: Having heard Rāghava's auspicious words, adorned with refinement, Agastya, slightly surprised, spoke to Rāghava.
verses.9: In ancient times, Prajapati Brahma, who was born from water and a lotus, first created the waters and then created various beings for their protection.
verses.10: Those beings, afflicted by hunger, thirst, and fear, humbly approached their creator and asked, "What shall we do?"
verses.11: Prajapati, the giver of honor, addressed those beings as if with a smile and instructed them with effort, "Protect!"
verses.12: Among those beings, some said, "We will protect," while others said, "We will eat"; then, having heard these responses from the hungry and the non-hungry, the creator of beings spoke to them.
verses.13: To those who said, "We will protect," he declared, "You shall be Rakshasas," and to those who said, "We will eat," he declared, "You shall indeed be Yakshas."
verses.14: There existed two demon lords, Heti and Praheti, who were brothers, vanquishers of foes, and resembled Madhu and Kaiṭabha.
verses.15: At that time, Praheti, being righteous, went to a hermitage, while Heti made a great effort to find a wife.
verses.16: That great-minded Heti, of immeasurable spirit, himself married a terrifying maiden named Bhaya, who was the sister of Kala (Death).
verses.17: Heti, the foremost among Rākṣasas and best among those with sons, begot a son named Vidyutkeśa in her (Bhaya).
verses.18: Vidyutkeśa, Heti's son, of great splendor and brilliance like the blazing sun, grew like a cloud in the midst of water.
verses.19: When the night-wanderer (Vidhyutkesha) attained auspicious youth, his father then resolved to perform his marriage ceremony.
verses.20: Then Heti, the chief of Rakshasas, sought Sandhya's daughter, who was equal to Sandhya in splendor, as a bride for his son.
verses.21: O Rama, Sandhya, having thought that her daughter must certainly be given to another, thus gave her daughter to Vidhyutkesha.
verses.22: Having obtained Sandhya's daughter, the night-wanderer Vidhyutkesha enjoyed with her, just as Maghavan (Indra) enjoys with Paulomi.
verses.23: O Rama, after some time, Salakatankata conceived from Vidhyutkesha, just as a line of clouds obtains moisture from the ocean.
verses.24: Then, that female demon, having gone to the Mandara mountain, gave birth to an offspring shining like a thundercloud, just as Ganga gave birth to the fire-born embryo (Kartikeya).
verses.25: Having abandoned her offspring, she, desiring union with Vidyutkesha, then enjoyed herself with her husband, completely forgetting her own son.
verses.26: The abandoned offspring, who had a roar like thunder and a luster like the autumn sun, then cried slowly, having placed his own fist in his mouth.
verses.27: Then Shiva, accompanied by Parvati and mounted on a bull, was traveling through the sky and heard the sound of crying.
verses.28: Shiva, the destroyer of Tripura, then saw the demon's son crying, accompanied by Uma, moved by Parvati's feeling of compassion.
verses.29: The imperishable and immutable Lord Mahadeva made that son of the demon, Sukesha, immortal and equal in age to his mother.
verses.30: To please Parvati, Shiva gave him a city that could move in the sky, and O son of the king, Uma also granted a boon to the demons.
verses.31: The boon granted by Uma was that conception would be immediate, birth would be immediate, and the child would immediately attain an age equal to that of its mother.
verses.32: Then, Sukesha, proud of the boon and having obtained glory from the presence of Lord Shiva, roamed everywhere, great and of great intellect, just as Indra does after obtaining his celestial city. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुर्थः सर्गः ।। 4 ।। Thus ends the fourth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
